reviewDecisions.rationale: Independent global evidence indicates structural DRAM scarcity and supplier bargaining power likely to persist beyond a single quarter.
Mature-semiconductor recovery is supportive context but does not independently define a more specific expectation gap than the niche-memory shortage thesis.
Record copper prices provide a quantified market signal consistent with structural supply tightness.
A major producer's lower production goal independently supports constrained mine supply.
Record US imports and growing buyer acceptance of Congolese copper create a distinct market-access change relevant to DRC producers.
Producer price increases are visible, but cautious downstream purchasing makes the earnings bridge too dependent on supply/cost discipline rather than verified end demand.
The physical shortage is real but dominated by conflict/logistics; a durable company-specific A-share expectation gap is not cleanly identifiable.
AI/data-center power demand remains strong, but the broad power-capex narrative is already highly visible and this item does not create a new company-specific edge.
